content:
Continuing the enumeration from
\[
x=\frac{l+2}{lk-4},\qquad lk-4\mid l+2,\qquad lk>4.
\]

Since \(2y+1\) and \(2x+1\) are odd, \(k,l,x,y\) must all be odd.

- If \(k=1\), then \(l-4\mid l+2\), so \(l-4\mid 6\). Thus \(l-4=1,3\), giving
  \[
  (x,y)=(7,3),(3,1).
  \]
- If \(k\ge 3\), then \(lk-4\le l+2\), so \(l(k-1)\le 6\). Since \(k\) is odd, \(k\ge 3\), hence \(l\le 3\).
  - For \(l=1\), \(k-4\mid 3\), so \(k=5,7\), giving
    \[
    (x,y)=(3,7),(1,3).
    \]
  - For \(l=3\), \(3k-4\mid 5\), so only \(k=3\), giving
    \[
    (x,y)=(1,1).
    \]

Thus the vertices are
\[
(1,1),(1,3),(3,1),(3,7),(7,3).
\]
Arranged convexly as
\[
(1,1),(3,1),(7,3),(3,7),(1,3),
\]
the shoelace area is
\[
\frac12\left|(1\cdot1+3\cdot3+7\cdot7+3\cdot3+1\cdot1)
-(1\cdot3+1\cdot7+3\cdot3+7\cdot1+3\cdot1)\right|
\]
\[
=\frac12|69-29|=20.
\]
Therefore the maximum possible area is
\[
\boxed{20}.
\]
